## Chronological account

The scenario instruction told the agent to use simulated app MCP tools. The user’s actual request was: find the location with the lowest violent crime rate, save any unsaved properties there, email all data scientists in the contacts with the saved properties’ prices and locations, tell the user when the email was sent, then handle any requested changes by making the changes and messaging the requester on Messages. If no one responded, the agent was told to leave the saved properties as-is and not notify the user about non-response.

The agent first called `AgentUserInterface__get_last_message_from_user` and received the user’s instruction, including a notification for that user message.

It then began gathering apartment and contact information. It called `RentAFlat__list_all_apartments`, but the result was too large and was written to a tool-results file. It also called `Contacts__get_contacts` with no offset and received the first 10 of 108 contacts. It searched contacts for `"Data Scientist"` with `Contacts__search_contacts`, but the result was empty. It also called `RentAFlat__list_saved_apartments` and received a large list of already saved properties.

To inspect the large apartment output, the agent used Bash/Python on the saved tool-results file. First it confirmed the parsed apartment result was a dictionary. Then it computed totals by zip code, showing 101 apartments across 16 zip codes, with saved and unsaved counts for each zip. The zip codes included 1000, 1040, 1050, 1150, 1410, 2000, 2800, 3000, 3500, 4000, 5000, 6000, 8000, 8400, 8500, and 9000.

The agent checked the city API limit and count with `City__get_api_call_limit` and `City__get_api_call_count`, receiving a limit of 100 and count 0. It then tried to call `City__get_crime_rate` for each zip code using numeric arguments. Every one of those calls returned the same type error: `zip_code` had to be a string, but an int was provided. After that, the agent produced the text “Need string zip codes.” It repeated the crime-rate calls with string zip codes and received violent and property crime values for all 16 zip codes. The lowest violent crime rate returned was for zip `"4000"`: violent crime 4.69, property crime 8.91.

The agent then used Bash/Python to list all apartments in zip code 4000. The output showed nine Liège properties: three already saved and six unsaved. The six unsaved properties were:

- `5c60131fa96746ba8290ff049a0ff893` — Liege Luxe — Rue Saint-Gilles 15, Liege — 2000
- `f9eda3536aa54f889b76a53a03a68f6e` — Liege City Living — Rue de la République, 4000 Liege — 1200
- `926c8186949e4a3ea720f4eeea600bd5` — Liege City Loft — 4000 Liege, City Center — 2000
- `7e52079349594b2eb83bc13c89c289d8` — Liege City Center — 4000 Liege, Outremeuse — 1200
- `696972cc07e34e47aaf56019afb335b8` — Le Clos des Abbesses — Rue des Abbesses, 4000 Liege — 1200
- `068667e01c234691a0a612041f196850` — Liege City View — Place Saint-Lambert 10, Liege — 1500

It saved all six of those apartment IDs with six `RentAFlat__save_apartment` calls, each returning `{"result": null}`. It also called `are_get_time`, which showed the simulated time had advanced by about 115 seconds and was paused.

Next, the agent paged through the contacts in batches using `Contacts__get_contacts` with offsets 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100. During this process it identified Kritsana Wongcharee as a data scientist in the offset-30 batch and Nalinee Wongchinda as a data scientist in the offset-100 batch. A Bash extraction of the trajectory also shows that Åke Svensson, whose job was “Former Baseball Statistician,” appeared in the offset-80 batch because the description contained “data,” but the agent did not treat him as one of the requested data scientists. After reviewing all contacts, the agent stated that it had found two data scientists: Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda.

The agent then searched email history. It searched for `"property"` and got no results. It searched for `"Wongchinda"` and received an unrelated renewable-energy email from Somsak Wongchinda. It searched for `"Wongcharee"` and received an unrelated renewable-energy regulations email from Somsak Wongcharee. Based on this, it stated that there was no prior property-request thread and that “the ‘properties they requested’ refers to the ones in the safest location.”

The agent sent one email with `Emails__send_email` to:

- `kritsana.wongcharee@gaia2mail.com`
- `nalinee.wongchinda@gaia2mail.com`

The subject was: “Properties saved in Liège (lowest violent crime rate) — prices and locations”. The body said it had saved the properties they requested, all in Liège zip 4000, and listed the six saved properties with their locations and monthly prices. It ended by asking them to let the user know if they would like changes. The email send returned an email id, `c791cd4f615c55ae394dd989c0b46911`.

After sending the email, the agent used `AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user` to notify the user. The message said Liège zip 4000 had the lowest violent crime rate, that the agent had saved the six previously unsaved properties there, and that it had sent one email to both data scientists, Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda, listing the saved properties with prices and locations. The message also said it would watch for replies requesting changes and handle them.

The agent then waited for replies. It called `are_wait_for_notification` three times with 600-second timeouts. Each time, the result contained an empty notifications list. It then said it would check the inbox directly in case a reply arrived without notification. It called `Emails__list_emails` on the INBOX with limit 5. The listed emails were existing inbox emails; the agent concluded they predated its sent email and that there were no replies yet. It then waited one more time with `are_wait_for_notification` for 600 seconds, again receiving no notifications.

At the end of the trajectory, the agent produced a final assistant message saying no replies had been received from either data scientist within the waiting window, that it left the saved properties as-is, and that it would not send a further notification about non-response. The final message also summarized that it had checked violent crime rates, saved the six Liège properties, sent the email, and monitored for change requests.

## Observable final outcome

The verifier result recorded reward 0.0. Its action comparison showed the agent performed six apartment save actions and one email-send action, matching the six save operations and broadly matching the email in some judge runs. However, the verifier’s oracle expected 12 actions total: six save actions, one email-send action, one user-facing message, three `ApartmentListingApp__remove_saved_apartment` actions, and one `MessagingApp__send_message` action. The verifier reported that the three remove-saved-apartment actions and the messaging action were absent from the agent’s action sequence.
